theorem schemeOpenModuleImage_pullback_exists
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U V : X.Opens) (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    {Z : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)}
    (b : Z ⟶ (schemeOpenModuleImage X U).obj M)
    (c : Z ⟶ (schemeOpenModuleImage X V).obj M)
    (hbc : b ≫ (schemeOpenModuleImageRestriction X
      (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U))).app M =
      c ≫ (schemeOpenModuleImageRestriction X
        (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V))).app M) :
    ∃ l : Z ⟶ M,
      l ≫ (schemeOpenModuleAdjunction X U).unit.app M = b ∧
      l ≫ (schemeOpenModuleAdjunction X V).unit.app M = c

title: Existence of an amalgamation for compatible open restrictions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U,V$ be open subsets with $U\cup V=X$, and let $M,Z$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $A$, let $M_A=j_{A*}r_A M$ and $\eta_A:M\to M_A$ be the transported restriction/direct-image unit of [def-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-data]. Let $\rho_{A,W}:M_A\to M_W$ be the nested-open restriction of [def-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-data]. If $b:Z\to M_U$ and $c:Z\to M_V$ satisfy $\rho_{U,U\cap V}\circ b=\rho_{V,U\cap V}\circ c$, then there exists $l:Z\to M$ with $\eta_U\circ l=b$ and $\eta_V\circ l=c$.

proof.text: Cancel the image of overFunctorEquiv.inv in each transported unit. The ordinary unit is section restriction. For sections over T, equality of the two unit images implies equality by TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq₂ on U intersection T and V intersection T. This proves unit_sections_injective directly, without an unproved uniqueness theorem.

Use the nested-open section restriction formula to transport compatible image sections to compatible sections on P=U intersection T and Q=V intersection T. Their union is T. Apply TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' with the Bool-indexed two-open cover to obtain x in M(T). Cancel the comparison isomorphisms to obtain both transported-unit equations.

Evaluate the morphism compatibility equation at T and z to obtain a section amalgamation. Choose its unique amalgamation f(T,z); the previous separatedness proof establishes uniqueness. Applying the two units shows that f respects addition and scalar multiplication. Naturality of b, c, and the units shows that f commutes with restriction, again by separatedness. Assemble these linear maps into a SheafOfModules morphism, and prove the two requested composite equations by componentwise extensionality.
